name: Jeff Ulbrich

views.text: Players should understand the defense well enough to solve problems themselves, without trick calls to bail them out.
Fundamentals, technique, effort and toughness come before any wrinkle.
Defensive linemen are fresher and better on fewer snaps, so rotate them.
When the defense struggles, coaches look at their own teaching and drills first.
A team that is not playing to its talent needs honest self-evaluation and to pull together.
Character matters as much as talent when adding players to a locker room.

signatures: saves his loudest energy for celebrating good plays rather than yelling at bad ones
praises specific players' competitiveness by name when asked about the unit
credits the head coach who gave him his chance when talking about his career
want: to be the gritty former backup who becomes a head coach on the strength of a tough, simple defense
fear: that a season of struggles makes people forget the defenses he built
voice: Intense but not a yeller; he speaks with the conviction of a ten-year special-teams linebacker and players listen. He is enthusiastic, quick to praise players and humble about coaches' responsibility for mistakes. He talks in terms of toughness, simplicity and honest self-evaluation.

evidence.summary: He wants a defense built on fundamentals, technique, effort and toughness, avoids gimmicks that rescue mistakes, and wants players to understand it well enough to solve problems. Intense but not a yeller, patient in teaching, high energy for celebrations; Saleh calls him genuine and passionate. Team site.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press (Dennis Waszak Jr.), via ClickOrlando
evidence.summary: AP profile on his promotion to interim head coach: a tough, blue-collar former 49ers linebacker whose words carry weight with players; Atlanta assistant and coordinator before joining Saleh in 2021; credits Saleh for his chance; the Jets blocked a 2023 interview request; he tells the team to unite and evaluate itself honestly. The promotion postdates the seed's frame.

He praises the character of new players, wants defensive linemen limited to about 30-35 snaps for health and performance, and says coaches must examine their own teaching and drills. Upbeat, player-praising tone. Team site.

Reflecting on an injury- and COVID-hit 2021 with a young roster, he expects more depth and schematic flexibility while keeping a fast, aggressive identity; candid about setbacks without dwelling. Team site.

As interim head coach he moves offensive play-calling from Hackett to Downing and says Rodgers backed it. Shows a decisive staff move; it postdates the seed's frame, where he is still defensive coordinator.
